interactions.summary: The reading describes the mountain's quake, the shouted Gloria, and Dante's intense curiosity about the unexplained event.

Jiang pauses to interpret the quake, connect Hugh Capet to later Petrine criticism, and prepare the class for Statius by contrasting Virgil's ecstatic response to Sordello with the opposite response he is about to have here.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang lecture with brief student recall prompts.

interactions.summary: The reading introduces Statius, has Virgil explain his limited role as guide, and gives the purgatorial account of why the mountain shakes at all.

claims.claim: The quake and Gloria are presented as collective signs that provoke Dante's strongest desire yet to understand what is happening on the mountain.
Jiang reads Hugh Capet's self-condemnation as symmetrical with Paradise's Peter attacking the Church and says the mountain quakes whenever a soul completes purgation and is released toward heaven.
Jiang primes the class to notice that Statius worships Virgil more intensely than Sordello did, yet Virgil will react in the opposite way.
Virgil explains that he can guide Dante only as far as his teaching reaches, because Dante's soul cannot yet ascend alone and Virgil himself remains excluded from blessed assembly.
Statius says purgatory above the gate is exempt from ordinary weather and geological disturbance, and that the mountain trembles only when a soul feels itself cleansed enough to rise higher.

signature_moments.moment: The universe celebrates a completed purgation with an earthquake rather than with a private inner feeling alone.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the universe celebrates with an earthquake
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It externalizes salvation into a cosmic event and makes the mountain itself morally alive.

signature_moments.moment: Virgil defines the reach of pagan wisdom by saying he can lead Dante only as far as his teaching reaches.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I shall lead him just as far as where I teach can reach
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is a compact statement of Virgil's greatness and limit at once.

signature_moments.moment: The mountain is described as so ordered that no perturbation touches it except the moral liberation of a soul.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it only trembles here when some soul feels its cleanse
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The entire environment becomes keyed to purification rather than to blind natural causation.

chronology_notes.note: This packet records Jiang's June 26 setup for the Statius encounter by explicitly forecasting an inversion of Virgil's earlier Sordello vanity scene.
